messages:
Maria K (Customer): Hey support, our app started getting JSON parse errors from the structured-output endpoint. Some responses are malformed — looks like fragments from multiple responses got mixed. Example attached below, request_id=req_abc123 trace=trace-987
Alex S (Support): Sorry you're seeing that — can you paste the raw response you got and confirm hosted/dedicated/private and model+SDK version?
Maria K (Customer): Hosted (us-east), model: redwood/gpt-4o-inf, SDK 1.3.2. Raw response samples: we call /v1/generate with json_mode=true and bulk inputs. Sometimes we get perfectly fine JSON per item, other times the response is unparseable. Example raw chunk we saved: 
```
{"id":1, "result": {"name": "Alice", "age": 30}}
{"id":2, "result": {"name": "Bob", "age": 25}}
```
But what our parser receives is sometimes concatenated or interleaved like: 
```
{"id":1, "result": {"name": "Alice", "age": 30}}{"id":2, "result": {"name": "Bob", "age": 25}}
```
and other times we see fields from object 2 copied into object 1: `{"id":1, "result": {"name": "Alice", "age": 25}}` which causes schema validation failures.
Alex S (Support): Thanks. Do you use streaming? Any client-side concurrency/parallel requests or retries? Also can you include response headers (x-rw-batch-id, x-rw-cache-hit, x-rw-trace)?
Maria K (Customer): We use the bulk endpoint (one HTTP call with an array of prompts). We do have client-side retry on 429/5xx. We saw no 5xx in these incidents, all 200. Sample headers from one response: `x-rw-batch-id: bat-42`, `x-rw-cache-hit: true` for first item, `x-rw-cache-hit: false` for the second, `x-rw-trace: trace-987`.
Alex S (Support): Hmm that cache-hit mismatch + same batch id is suspicious. Looping eng. @Jason P can you take a look?
Jason P (Eng): I'll pick this up. Quick Qs: any latency spikes when this happens? Also can you share a minimal repro (curl or small script) that reliably fails?
Maria K (Customer): Latency is normal ~120-200ms. I can repro ~1/200 requests with our production load but reproduced more reliably by sending 8 concurrent prompts in one bulk call and setting client batch size to 8. I'll paste a minimized curl reproducer: 
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/bulk/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"json_mode":true, "inputs": ["prompt1","prompt2","prompt3","prompt4","prompt5","prompt6","prompt7","prompt8"]}' \
  -D - \
| sed -n '1,200p'
```
Run that in a loop and occasionally the output is invalid JSON.
Jason P (Eng): Thanks. Reproduced locally by running 1000 loops with similar payloads. Seeing some responses where two JSON lines are concatenated without delimiter and in others partial fields are swapped. Looking at router logs, I see entries where a cached prefix (x-rw-cache-hit=true) is returned for one routed shard and fresh batch responses for another — the per-request KV cache key was colliding across concurrent requests during the batch window.
Tara L (Oncall): FYI we deployed batching rewrite (commit abcdef1) last week that changed cache key scoping. Rolling this to staging to confirm.
Jason P (Eng): Root cause hypothesis: request-scoped KV/cache was mistakenly made shard-global within the micro-batch window. With highly concurrent bulk requests, a cached prefix for a previous request could be inserted into the outgoing stream for an unrelated request inside the same batch. That produces the observed "crosstalk" where JSON fragments from different responses appear in one stream.
Maria K (Customer): Ugh that makes sense. Any workaround we can apply right now? We're hitting schema validation in prod.
Alex S (Support): Short-term mitigations: 1) set `enable_prefix_cache=false` in your request to bypass server prefix cache; 2) reduce `batch_window_ms` to 0 to force per-request flushing; 3) temporary: set `max_batch_size=1` to avoid multi-request batching. Jason, is SDK 1.3.3 patched?
Jason P (Eng): Yes, we have a hotfix in SDK 1.3.3 that uses request-scoped cache keys and avoids cross-batch reuse. Server-side fix is in PR #789 to correct the router scoping and add tests; planning canary tomorrow. Workarounds Alex listed are correct.
Maria K (Customer): I toggled `enable_prefix_cache=false` and ran the same loop — errors stopped immediately. But we did ~12k extra requests due to retries earlier; can we get credits for that?
Alex S (Support): We'll escalate billing for credit consideration. Please DM me invoice IDs / request samples and I'll open the billing case.
DeployBot: Started rollback test of commit abcdef1 in staging at 1764005300.
Tara L (Oncall): Action items: 1) Jason will finish PR #789 and request a canary tomorrow (ETA 24h). 2) Support will share recommended temporary config with customer and offer credits review. 3) Engineering will add e2e test that simulates high-concurrency bulk requests and asserts json demarcation.
Jason P (Eng): PR linked in thread, tests added. We'll monitor canary metrics (x-rw-json-errors) and batch-mismatch rate.
Maria K (Customer): Great, disabling prefix cache fixed our immediate pain. Thanks for fast triage. Please loop me when canary is green. +1 for credits consideration. :pray:
Alex S (Support): Noted — I'll follow up on billing + reopen if you see any regression. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
